title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — will explain; does not impugn mediate/consequent imputation after corruption
pass_a_gloss: Tip: Placeus will unpack the argument's force. He marks what he is not attacking—mediate/consequent imputation after each one's existence and corruption—before the immediate/antecedent target. Tip before that explanation.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Since the learned man could not see the force of this reason, I will explain it. Let the reader remember, if he will, that I am not attacking mediate or consequent imputation, which is later than each one's existence and corruption.
source_text: PLAC. Quandoquidem videre huius rationis vim Vir doctus non potuit, eam explicabo. Meminerit igitur, Lector, si placet, me non impugnare imputationem mediatam seu consequentem, quae cuiusque existentia & corruptione posterior est.
notes: Cap. IX Rom5 omnes densify section 622 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 349–351 tip).
